title: Cobalt Horizon — Highway Airline OOH
description: A 14:5 billboard template engineered for 70-mph legibility: one full-bleed sky photograph, a three-word bone-white headline ranged hard left, and a coral logo lockup anchored in the right 20%. Text never crosses into the image area.
philosophy: This template treats constraint as the entire design language. It exists because outdoor airline advertising collapses under the weight of too many words and too many colors — so it enforces one photograph, three words, one logo, two type colors, and nothing else. It refuses overlay text, supporting copy, decorative treatments, and any layout element that asks for more than a single glance. It is made for advertising directors who accept that a roadside billboard either lands in half a second or is invisible forever.
goodFor: Three-word airline taglines set at extreme display scale
Highway, motorway, and roadside outdoor advertising placements
Wide-format airport terminal corridor and jetbridge backdrops
Regional carrier brand campaigns anchored by a single strong hero photograph
avoidFor: Multi-bullet pitch or sales decks requiring body copy
Chart-heavy or data-dense quarterly business reviews
Social media square or portrait-crop format adaptations
Small-screen or mobile viewing contexts where the 14:5 ratio collapses
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a single held breath at cruising altitude — vast, spare, and moving at speed. A sky photograph of cinematic scale dominates the right two-thirds, its horizon line threading the frame to draw the eye toward the headline. The left panel is a hard editorial wall: three words, commanding and immovable. Avoid gradient overlays on the photograph or any decorative secondary elements — all tension lives between the typographic block and the sweeping sky beyond it.
examples.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="sky" x1="0.5" y1="0" x2="0.5" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#ebe6e0"/>
      <stop offset="42%" stop-color="#ebe6e0"/>
      <stop offset="58%" stop-color="#e85a2f"/>
      <stop offset="66%" stop-color="#e85a2f"/>
      <stop offset="78%" stop-color="#52514f"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1a1a1c"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <clipPath id="skyClip">
      <rect x="720" y="0" width="1200" height="1080"/>
    </clipPath>
  </defs>

  <!-- Full-bleed base -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1920" height="1080" fill="#1a1a1c"/>

  <!-- Right two-thirds: cinematic sky photograph -->
  <rect x="720" y="0" width="1200" height="1080" fill="url(#sky)"/>

  <!-- High-altitude cirrus / contrails threading toward the headline -->
  <g clip-path="url(#skyClip)" fill="#ebe6e0">
    <ellipse cx="1720" cy="246" rx="320" ry="5"/>
    <ellipse cx="1380" cy="298" rx="260" ry="4"/>
    <ellipse cx="1020" cy="352" rx="180" ry="3"/>
    <ellipse cx="1560" cy="410" rx="210" ry="4"/>
    <ellipse cx="1820" cy="470" rx="140" ry="3"/>
    <ellipse cx="1180" cy="500" rx="120" ry="2"/>
  </g>

  <!-- Horizon thread — subtle burn band echoing the sunset -->
  <rect x="720" y="636" width="1200" height="1" fill="#1a1a1c" opacity="1"/>

  <!-- Cloud deck silhouette below horizon -->
  <g clip-path="url(#skyClip)">
    <path d="M 720 860 Q 900 820 1080 850 T 1440 845 T 1800 855 T 1920 850 L 1920 1080 L 720 1080 Z" fill="#1a1a1c" opacity="1"/>
  </g>

  <!-- Left 37.5%: solid editorial wall -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="720" height="1080" fill="#1a1a1c"/>

  <!-- Three-word headline, stacked, hard left, maximum display scale -->
  <g font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-weight="700" fill="#ebe6e0">
    <text x="58" y="330" font-size="210" textLength="604" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs" letter-spacing="-8">HOLD.</text>
    <text x="58" y="590" font-size="210" textLength="604" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs" letter-spacing="-8">THE.</text>
    <text x="58" y="850" font-size="210" textLength="604" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs" letter-spacing="-8">HORIZON.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Logo lockup, pinned at optical midheight in rightmost 20% -->
  <g transform="translate(1556, 540)">
    <circle cx="0" cy="-2" r="17" fill="none" stroke="#1a1a1c" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <line x1="-28" y1="-2" x2="28" y2="-2" stroke="#1a1a1c" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <text x="46" y="5" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="21" font-weight="800" fill="#1a1a1c" letter-spacing="4.5">COBALT HORIZON</text>
  </g>
</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: Extreme 14:5 horizontal canvas, edge-to-edge bleed with zero outer margin. Left ~35% of the billboard is a solid-panel text zone: the three-word headline anchors hard left at maximum display scale, stacked one word per line, with a shallow left-edge inset only. Right ~65% is entirely consumed by the full-bleed sky photograph, with the logo lockup pinned at optical midheight inside the rightmost 20% — the two zones never overlap. No page number, no footer band, no rule lines, no supporting copy of any kind.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like velocity frozen — wide open sky or low-horizon runway tarmac giving the composition overwhelming headroom and forward thrust. Asymmetric tension between the vast photographic left and the tightly controlled brand right channels the eye in a single unbroken pull-through. Mood is stripped and altitude-confident: bold, unhurried, with no decorative warmth or competing focal points. Avoid texture overlays, gradient washes, and any visual element that requires more than a half-second to resolve.

    <!-- main wing -->

  <!-- Hairline vertical rule between message column and brand strip (78%) -->
  <rect x="1497" y="60" width="1" height="960" fill="#52514f"/>

  <!-- Brand strip background (right 22%) -->
  <rect x="1498" y="0" width="422" height="1080" fill="#1a1a1c"/>

  <!-- ============ PRIMARY MESSAGE — three words, upper-center third of left zone ============ -->
  <g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" fill="#1a1a1c">
    <text x="80" y="250" font-size="236" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-8">SKY</text>
    <text x="80" y="430" font-size="236" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-8" fill="#e85a2f">MEETS</text>
    <text x="80" y="610" font-size="236" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-8">ROAD.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ============ BRAND LOCKUP (top of right strip) ============ -->
  <!-- Mark: simple chevron -->
  <g transform="translate(1560,140)">
    <path d="M 0 60 L 60 0 L 120 60 L 96 60 L 60 24 L 24 60 Z" fill="#e85a2f"/>
  </g>
  <text x="1560" y="290" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="58" font-weight="800" fill="#ebe6e0" letter-spacing="2">COBALT</text>
  <text x="1560" y="350" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="58" font-weight="300" fill="#ebe6e0" letter-spacing="2">HORIZON</text>

  <!-- Hairline divider inside brand column -->
  <rect x="1560" y="402" width="300" height="1" fill="#52514f"/>

  <!-- Secondary callout — single route identifier -->
  <g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" fill="#ebe6e0">
    <text x="1560" y="470" font-size="18" font-weight="600" letter-spacing="6" fill="#52514f">NONSTOP</text>
    <text x="1560" y="560" font-size="72" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-2">LAX</text>
    <text x="1560" y="560" font-size="72" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-2" fill="#e85a2f" dx="140">→</text>
    <text x="1720" y="560" font-size="72" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-2">JFK</text>
    <text x="1560" y="610" font-size="22" font-weight="400" letter-spacing="3" fill="#ebe6e0">FROM $149 ONE-WAY</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Campaign code — flush bottom-right inside brand column -->
  <text x="1880" y="1030" text-anchor="end" font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="16" fill="#52514f" letter-spacing="2">CH-OOH-26 / FL 0422</text>
</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: The 14:5 canvas bleeds edge-to-edge; a hard vertical partition at roughly the 78% horizontal mark reserves the rightmost strip exclusively for the brand lockup plus one secondary callout — a single route identifier, stat, or CTA line. The primary message occupies the left zone, anchored to the upper-center third of that area and strictly non-overlapping with the brand strip. A hairline vertical rule marks the boundary between message and brand columns; no footer band spans the full width, but a campaign code or flight number may sit flush bottom-right inside the brand column.
